category: managed Postgres and friends with a free plan that powers off on inactivity

free_tier.stated: Free plan with 1 GB RAM and 1 GB total storage per service, on Postgres, MySQL, Valkey, Kafka and OpenSearch; free indefinitely with no time limit, but the service powers off after a period of inactivity

retention.stated: the service powers off after a period of inactivity, on three triggers: no initial usage in the first few hours, or no continuative activity later; a powered-off service is deleted after 180 days. The Free plan is the exception to 'data retention is only limited by storage'

egress.terms: no egress allowance, quota or per-GB rate is published on the free-plan pages or the PostgreSQL pricing table; recorded as a gap after checking both

interface_detail: the Postgres wire protocol; an API and the avn CLI
tooling: psql and any Postgres client; the avn CLI
chaining: the free service powers off after periods of inactivity, and the smallest paid step is the Developer tier at USD 5 a month for PostgreSQL and MySQL: a dedicated single node with 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM and 8 GB storage, always on, with a daily backup, Basic support and networking included, but no point-in-time recovery, high availability or uptime SLA

limits.value: 1 GB total storage per service; 1 GB RAM
the free service powers off after a period of inactivity; a service powered off for more than 180 days is automatically deleted
max_connections is set to 20 on a free PostgreSQL service, and there is no connection pooling

identity_cost.detail: email signup; no card on the Free plan

reliability_note: free services power off on inactivity and a service powered off for more than 180 days is automatically deleted; a powered-off service for a version past end of life is deleted within 7 days
confidence_note: three first-party Aiven pages were read on 2026-10-22. The pricing page gives 1 GB RAM and 1 GB storage. The free-PostgreSQL page gives the inactivity power-off. The service power-cycle page gives the 180-day deletion. The pricing page's 'with the exception of Free plan' clause is a carve-out and not boilerplate. The free tier is what it carves out.

evidence.proved: Free column: RAM per VM 1 GB, Total storage 1 GB; Developer USD 5 with 8 GB; Hobbyist from USD 12; 'Data retention is only limited by storage, with the exception of Free plan'

'Service powers off after a period of inactivity (you'll be notified by email and in-platform beforehand)'; 'It's free indefinitely with no time limit, but the service is automatically powered off after a period of inactivity'

two power-off triggers: 'Power off free services with no initial usage within the first few hours after the service is running' and 'Power off free services with no continuative activity on the service'
'Services powered off for more than 180 days are automatically deleted'; the 180-day grace does not apply to an end-of-life version, which is deleted within 7 days
'Developer tier services are not automatically powered off when inactive'; the paid step is what removes the clock
'No connection pooling' and '`max_connections` limit set to `20`' on the free tier

the smallest paid step is the Developer tier at USD 5/month; the same page lists 1 CPU, 1 GB RAM, 8 GB storage, always-on, daily backups, Basic support and networking included, and no PITR, high availability or uptime SLA
evidence.quote: The Developer Tier is a dedicated, single-node PostgreSQL or MySQL database for $5 per month.

evidence.proved: the Developer tier is always on; the same page repeats the free-tier power-off triggers and the PostgreSQL Developer limits of no connection pooling and max_connections 20
evidence.quote: Developer tier services are not automatically powered off when inactive.

evidence.proved: the free PostgreSQL tier still has no connection pooling and sets max_connections to 20; the record's request-rate limit is unchanged
evidence.quote: No connection pooling ... `max_connections` limit set to `20`

notes: 1 GB is the smallest free Postgres storage in this class, and the free plan powers off on inactivity, so it does not answer the question the class was formed to ask. 5 GB is what the plan used to give and several comparison pages still print it. The paid Developer tier at USD 5 a month is the version of this that stays up: 'Developer tier services are not automatically powered off when inactive'.
binding_note: 1 GB of storage is small, but the inactivity power-off is what defeats the use a reader would pick this for: an unattended job that runs less often than the inactivity window. The 180-day deletion sets the outer limit.
